Commentary.Commentary: All is in readiness for the action to kick off in Ahmedabad for Day 3! Both umpires have walked out, and the Indian players come out and form a huddle, led by their skipper, Shubman Gill, who is giving a pep talk. Now, they disperse to take their respective positions. Also, the two openers of the West Indies stride out, where Tagenarine Chanderpaul will open the innings alongside John Campbell, and they both have a big task ahead. India are starting with the spearhead, Jasprit Bumrah. With three slips and a gully in place, Bumrah to Campbell. Here we go...

JUST IN -  India have declared overnight for 448/5 with a lead of 286 runs and want to use the early moisture of the pitch as they have put the Windies to bat right from the start of the play on Day 3. As it was expected and now, there is an uphill task for the batters of the West Indies to bat out and chop down this massive deficit, while Indian bowlers will look to bowl them out and win the first Test with an innings. Surely, an exciting day is on the cards for all of us!

Pitch Report - Daren Ganga and Deep Dasgupta are pitchside with their analysis. Deep notes that Day 3 is the ‘moving day’ in Test cricket, with bright sunshine and pleasant conditions. Recalls that Day 1 aided the fast bowlers with 12 wickets, Day 2 belonged to the batters with over 300 runs, and now expects plenty in it for the spinners. Daren joins and observes that three centurions on Day 2 handled the surface smartly - Rahul with assured footwork, Jurel using the crease, and Jadeja advancing down the track. Points to rough patches that will interest spinners like Jadeja, Sundar, and Kuldeep, and urges West Indies batters to take lessons and show belief. Dasgupta concludes that batting remains possible, but only with application, as spinners now have far more to work with from the footmarks.

The pitch? Still good for batting, with a touch of wear for the spinners to exploit. Expect Jadeja and Kuldeep to enjoy themselves when it’s India’s turn with the ball. The weather is hot, humid, and draining, which will test the physical strength again as it did in two days. Tactically, it’s clear - India want domination, while the West Indies want time in the middle. Day 3 will be the real ‘make or break’ day, so hop on with us for ball-by-ball coverage throughout the day!

Meanwhile, the West Indies? What do they want? Pride and resilience - that’s what they need. Batting hasn’t clicked, but they’ve got players like Hope, Athanaze, Chase and King who can dig deep. If they can put up a fight, even just take the game into Day 4, it’ll be a small win after the pounding so far. Their bowlers need quick strikes early today - Jadeja and Sundar are still at the crease - and their batters must learn from the patience Rahul showed. Otherwise, this Test could finish in three days flat!

Now, what does India want on Day 3? Options, plenty of them. They can declare before the start of play and let Bumrah and Siraj unleash the new cherry at West Indies' batters early in the morning. Or, they could stretch it further, pile another 80-100 runs, and bury Windies under scoreboard pressure. Tactically, India know the game is theirs to lose, as they just need to be smart about how quickly they want to go for the kill.

Day 2? That was a batting masterclass! Rahul brought up his first home Test hundred in around nine years, Jurel announced himself with a dreamy maiden Test ton, and Jadeja played the perfect all-rounder’s role with sword celebration and all. West Indies tried everything but Indian batters just wore them down. By stumps, 448/5 on the board, centuries in the bag, and the lead is nearly 300. For the Windies, it was a day of long, hard toil with very little to celebrate.

Let’s have a recap of the match so far. Day 1 was all about India’s bowlers setting the tone with pure fire. Siraj ripped through the top order, Bumrah was clinical, and Kuldeep spun webs in the middle overs. West Indies folded for just 162, and India’s openers began the reply cautiously. KL Rahul looked solid, Gill looked promising, and the hosts closed the day with a lead in sight. The tone was set, and India had their noses well ahead, while the visitors were already chasing the game.

Two days gone, and this Test has tilted firmly towards India, but… but test cricket never writes its script in just two acts! The hosts are ahead by a massive 286 runs, and their batting stars have feasted on a tiring West Indies attack. Rahul, Jurel, and Jadeja all struck hundreds and made it look like batting paradise, which it isn’t. Now, we are standing on the ‘Moving Day’. The big question is simple on Day 3 - will India pull the trigger on a declaration or bat even longer to bat the Windies out completely? Strap in, because this day could decide how long this contest lasts. On that note, hello and welcome to all of you!
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

India hold all the aces in this Test. As we head into Day 3, the big question is when the declaration will come or whether West Indies can seize a moment of momentum and take the five remaining wickets to wrest that declaration decision away from India. One school of thought suggests India could declare overnight, giving Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj the chance to exploit any early-morning assistance. Alternatively, they might prefer to keep the tourists out in the field for another session before piling on further pressure. It has been a chastening experience for a relatively inexperienced touring side, but they will need to show a stomach for a fight whenever they come out to bat. Saturday, 4th October, will be Day 3 of the Test, with the first ball scheduled for 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT). As always, we will be here nice and early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

KL Rahul is up for a quick chat, and he begins by reflecting on his form, saying that the last four to five months have been really good for him and he is enjoying his batting. Speaking about the break between the England series and this one, he mentions that the tour of England was fun, and after a long series there, the break has helped him feel fresh. Adds that he played a game last week with India A to get back into rhythm. On nerves, Rahul admits that he was a bit nervous since he hadn’t played for a while, but he managed to settle in. Talking about the conditions, he points out that it was physically challenging, though he is not entirely sure what to expect going forward. Highlights that the only thing he has worked on recently is maintaining his batting tempo. Signs off by revealing that his celebration after the hundred was dedicated to his daughter.

The second new ball was eventually taken early in the third session and was shared between Jayden Seales and Johann Layne. It proved to be a period of interrogation for the two Indian batters, but once the spinners came on, they quickly resumed their usual rhythm. First Jurel and then Jadeja brought up their centuries, with Dhruv recording a maiden Test hundred and Ravindra notching the sixth of his career as he continued his rich vein of form. Khary Pierre finally broke the 206-run stand by inducing an edge from Jurel, but Jadeja and Washington Sundar closed the day for the hosts with a 286-run lead.

Rahul fell immediately after the lunch break, but that setback did not deter Dhruv Jurel and Ravindra Jadeja from upping the tempo. Jadeja took the initiative before Jurel joined in on the act. Surprisingly, the West Indies delayed taking the second new ball, eventually opting for it 17 overs after it became available. Jayden Seales did find some reverse swing with the old ball during a short burst, which may have influenced the decision to hold off on the new cherry. However, once that movement faded, delaying the new ball only allowed Jadeja and Jurel to extend India’s advantage with little resistance.

Another dominant day at the office for India makes it two days in a row, and they have only gone and increased the gulf between the two sides. The West Indies endured 90 overs of long toil with only 3 wickets to show for their efforts, while India scored 327 runs in the day. The hosts began the day 41 runs behind, while the Windies were desperate to respond after a tough opening day. KL Rahul survived a heart-in-mouth moment in the very first over when an outside edge flew between the keeper and slip, but he soon settled in to register his second Test hundred at home, his first since 2016. Shubman Gill added a composed fifty as India moved into the lead.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! A serene first hour of the final session sees Dhruv Jurel and Ravindra Jadeja continue their fantastic work, extending their partnership to 146 runs and taking India’s lead to a commanding 202. Both batters picked up right where they left off before Tea, looking utterly settled and in no rush. Their measured approach in prioritising time at the crease over quick runs strongly suggests India are not eyeing a declaration yet. Instead, they'll want to bat through to the end of the day. Meanwhile, the West Indies bowlers toiled away to no avail. What’s perhaps more concerning for the tourists is their deteriorating body language. It has been discussed on air, and an observation rings true - the fielders appear disconsolate and resigned, a clear sign that the fight has gone out of the side and they’re simply waiting for the batters to make a mistake. The only question now is how far the partnership will go, and when we'll see a triple-figure score from both of these impressive players.

Commentary.Commentary: Back for the final session of Day 2! The players have walked back onto the outfield, taking their respective positions. Also, stride out the two unbeaten batters, Ravindra Jadeja and Dhruv Jurel, of India, who have both registered their respective fifties. Jomel Warrican will start the proceedings. Jomel to Dhruv. Here we go..
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Now, the hosts are in cruise control with Jadeja on yet another Test fifty, seven in his last nine innings - ridiculous consistency, and Jurel is celebrating his second Test fifty with a classy knock. India’s sights are firmly on a massive total. 400, maybe 500? before turning the screws. For the West Indies, the challenge is simple but massive - break this stand and find some momentum. Otherwise, the last session might see India bat them out of the game completely, or even unleash their bowlers late in the evening to clinch a couple of wickets. Session three promises plenty, which will start at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT).

Warrican did ask questions, and Seales worked hard with some reverse swing, but the wickets column didn’t budge. The big talking point, though, was West Indies holding back the second new ball for way too long. Still, they haven't taken it. Against two set batters, you’d think a harder ball might at least offer a breakthrough, but the hesitation allowed India to march on. Chase shuffled his bowlers, but with little penetration, frustration grew, and India kept piling on the runs.

Right after Lunch, the visitors got the wicket they desperately wanted - Rahul, after a gritty hundred, fell to Jomel Warrican’s tempting line outside off. That gave West Indies a sniff. But from there, the door that cracked open was shut firmly by Jadeja and Jurel. They didn’t rush at any point while they rotated, they defended when needed, and when the balls were in their arc, they punished them. The result? A partnership that’s already crossed the hundred mark and looks far from done.

Another session, another stamp of authority from India! They’ve now bossed all five sessions across two days, and the scoreboard screams it loud - 326/4, a lead of 164. From the moment KL Rahul fell early in this session, it’s been all about the calm, composed rebuilding from Ravindra Jadeja and Dhruv Jurel. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of the second session of the day. The two umpires and players make their way out to the centre. West Indies are starting with spin in the form of Jomel Warrican. KL Rahul to face the first ball. A slip and a short leg in place. Let's play...

Khary Pierre and Roston Chase occasionally found the rough, but most of the marks are outside the right-hander’s leg stump and therefore posed little threat. However, those areas could come into play later when the likes of Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar come out to bat. Starting the day 41 runs adrift, India have built a lead of 56 and could look to force the pace in the afternoon session. Play after Lunch is set to resume at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT). See you then. Cheers!

From there, the tourists struggled to create even half a chance through their pacers before turning to spin at both ends. Shubman Gill lifted the tempo, while KL Rahul continued to bat with his usual measured approach. The introduction of spin did allow the visiting side to regain some control. It was fifty and out for the Indian skipper, but Rahul remained solid as a rock and brought up his second home Test hundred towards the closing stages of the session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 29 overs, 97 runs and 1 wicket. Another session in this Test that has belonged to India. West Indies were made to work hard and still have plenty to do in the sessions to follow. The tourists were in search of early wickets, but their field placements from the outset suggested otherwise, as they were set up more to save runs than to attack. Jayden Seales found KL Rahul’s edge in the very first over of the day, but with only a solitary slip in place and positioned wide, the chance went begging.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! The first hour of Day 2 has seen a cautious start from the overnight pair, with both batters, KL Rahul and Shubman Gill, initially showing great restraint. However, as the session progressed and the pitch seemed to ease out, they began finding the boundaries more frequently in the last couple of overs. At the same time, the West Indies bowlers toiled hard and generated a couple of chances, inducing edges that frustratingly fell short or sped through the gaps, denying them the crucial breakthrough they needed as they continue their hard grind. Riding on the steady accumulation of runs, India successfully erased the first innings deficit early on Day 2. With the score at 174/2, India now have a lead over the West Indies by 12 runs. They would want to extend this to a considerable lead so that they don't have to bat again, while the Windies are looking for a breakthrough. Let's see how the final hour of the first session goes.

Commentary.Commentary: All is in readiness for the action to kick off in Ahmedabad for Day 2! The players of the West Indies walk out and form a huddle beside the boundary cushions, led by their skipper, Roston Chase. Also, stride out the two overnight Indian batters, where the skipper, Shubman Gill, will resume the innings alongside half-centurion, KL Rahul. Windies are starting with Jayden Seales straightaway, as they want wickets. One wide slip with a gully in place. Seales to Rahul. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is near the deck. He mentions that the sun is out and it is a beautiful morning in Ahmedabad, with clear skies in contrast to yesterday’s overcast conditions. Shares that on Day 1, the average seam movement measured 0.8 degrees in the first session, 0.5 in the second, and 0.4 in the third. Adds that there is visible wear and tear on both sides of the wicket, which could trouble batters as the game progresses. Daren reckons that Day 2 could be less about seam and more about spin. Deep Dasgupta joins him, and he opines that the red-soil surface always offers something for the bowlers. Believes that the first two sessions today should provide the best conditions for batting, and if the batters show application, there are runs to be had.

So, what’s in store for Day 2? India want control, and they’ll dream of a lead of at least 200 from this point and total dominance so that they don’t have to bat again. At the same time, the West Indies want survival - early wickets, discipline, and keeping India under check. Fans, keep your snacks stocked, as the excitement is palpable. This day could flip from chill to chaos in a blink!

Now, about the pitch. What can we expect? It’s expected to flatten out and become friendly for the batters with very little grass. The 38-over-old ball in the morning can still do a bit, but once it softens even more, it’s going to be survival-of-the-fittest for the bowlers. The spinners might get some bite later in the day, but right now, it screams runs, runs, and more runs. The heat in Ahmedabad will also play a part - tiring bowlers faster, testing the fitness levels of the batters. Basically, the first two hours today? Extremely important for both sides in the context of momentum.

But wait, don’t count the West Indies out just yet! It's too early. Their batting may have flopped on Day 1, but the bowlers know this is their chance at redemption. Jayden Seales can get movement early, and if he finds his rhythm, Rahul and Gill will have to watch out. Roston Chase, along with Jomel Warrican and Khary Pierre’s spin, could become a handful trio once the sun bakes the pitch. And in the field, they need sharp catches, no freebies, as one drop could snatch the game from them. If the Windies can knock over two or three wickets before lunch, suddenly India will feel the heat.

For India, the plan is super clear - bat big, bat long, bat like kings. KL Rahul already looks calm as a monk, stroking the ball around as if cramps don’t exist, and he’s eyeing a big daddy hundred to set the tone. Shubman Gill? He’s settling in nicely, waiting to turn this start into something big. And the scary part? Behind them are stroke-makers and all-rounders galore - Jadeja, Sundar, Reddy, Jurel - players who can frustrate the bowlers for hours. If India bat through the day, they’ll stack up a massive lead and leave WI chasing shadows.

Day 2 is here but at the end of Day 1, India walked off like an absolute boss, only 41 runs behind with 8 wickets still in hand. Momentum? 100 percent blue. But hang on - this game isn’t over yet. The West Indies may have been knocked back early, but one hot spell of bowling in the morning, and suddenly the pressure swings. The pitch looks good but both teams know - today is when the real story of this Test match gets written. On that note, hello and welcome to all of you!
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

So, India clearly are in the driver’s seat, while the West Indies are chasing shadows. Can Rahul and Gill pile on the runs and stretch the lead? Or will Seales and the spinners somehow drag their side back? We’ll find out. The action resumes for Day 2 at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) on Friday, 3rd October. Join us an hour earlier for all the buildup and insights. Till then, take care! CIAO!

TRANSITION? Both teams are in that phase. The big positive - India’s transition players are stepping up. Bumrah and Siraj looked like they never left England, Kuldeep carried his Asia Cup form, and Jurel impressed behind the stumps. Rahul is in zen mode, who is looking for his second home Test hundred. For the West Indies, Seales was the lone bright spot, bowling with heart and rhythm. But their batting? Wobbly. Their bowling? Did well in patches but would be feeling the pressure.

But Jaiswal, after looking sharp with 36 runs, fell to Seales, undone by a ball too good to resist. Then Sai Sudharsan, scratchy from the start, wasted another opportunity and fell lbw to Chase. For a moment, Windies sensed an opening. But nope - KL Rahul was the wall. He notched a gritty fifty despite cramps in his left leg and anchored the innings with composure, while skipper Shubman Gill joined him - calm and solid. Both ensured no further damage was done. India closed at 121/2, just 41 runs shy.

Session 3 started with India’s openers walking in. At first? Cautious. Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul defended their way through, as Seales bowled with venom and got good support from Layne. Rain halted play at 23/0, but when the drizzle cleared, the batting intent changed gears. Rahul and Jaiswal pressed the accelerator and boundaries started to flow easily.

Session 2 didn’t bring salvation either. Roston Chase, Shai Hope, and Justin Greaves tried a mini-fightback, but Bumrah’s yorker knocked Greaves over, and the floodgates reopened. Siraj was gunning for a maiden fifer at home, but had to settle for four, while Kuldeep’s magic dismissed Hope and Warrican. Sundar chipped in with Pierre’s wicket, showing India’s bowling depth is unreal. In just 44.1 overs, the West Indies were folded for 162. From toss to Tea, it was India’s show.

Let's go through what happened on DAY 1. Session 1 was all about pace, fire, and mayhem. Bumrah started a bit leg-sided, but Siraj was dialled in from ball one. He wrecked the top order -  Chanderpaul nicking for a duck, Athanaze gone at slip, and Brandon King bowled in no time. Bumrah too joined in with Campbell’s scalp after a smart review. Dhruv Jurel’s sharp glovework kept the energy up, and by the time Lunch rolled in, West Indies were limping at 90/5. India owned the morning - clean, ruthless, and clinical.

STUMPS ON DAY 1! A day that shows INDIA'S DOMINANCE! First, with the ball and then calmly with the bat. West Indies won the toss, chose to bat, and then just… crumbled. From 90/5 at Lunch to 162 all out, their innings felt short, rushed, and disappointing. Mohammed Siraj and Jasprit Bumrah were the wrecking crew. Then came India’s reply with the bat - steady, calculated, and effective so far. At stumps, India sit pretty at 121/2, only 41 runs behind. Advantage? Huge. Pressure? All on Windies.
